guidance: Only letters and digits count. Capitals and small letters count as the same, and punctuation doesn't count.
On older pages the long s (ſ), which looks like an f without the bar across, counts as s. A reading with f in its place doesn't match.
If the box cuts off part of the word, look at the line above it to see the whole word.
If a letter is too worn or blotted to tell which reading it supports, pick Can't tell.

For a printed fraction such as ½ that neither reading has, pick Neither matches and type the word. The ⌨ button beside Send has ½ ¼ ¾ and other characters a keyboard lacks. 1/2 typed out counts the same.
intro: These come from English-language pages in Chronicling America, the Library of Congress's collection of historic American newspapers. Most are words where two machine readings disagree. Others ask whether a drawn line runs between two columns, or whether a machine reading missed part of a block of print. Each card says what to look for.
